## v0.44.0 — 2026-07-27

### Fixes
- **437:** scripts/ deterministically wins over scripts/assistant/ in sys.path (`40e051d`)
  > - setup.py:38 and gates.py:92 guarded their sys.path insert with
  >   `if _SCRIPTS_DIR not in sys.path`, which gate.sh's exported
  >   PYTHONPATH=scripts/ can satisfy trivially -- scripts/ ends up present
  >   but at sys.path[1], behind sys.path[0] (each file's own dir,
  >   scripts/assistant/), so the insert(0, ...) that's supposed to make
  >   scripts/ win gets skipped.
  > - That shadowing made setup.py's `import config as project_config`
  >   resolve scripts/assistant/config.py (the engine config module) instead
  >   of the shared scripts/config.py loader, dying with an AttributeError
  >   on every setup.py invocation under gate.sh's env -- the real root
  >   cause of #412's 43-fail setup-assistant cluster.
  > - Replace the conditional guard with remove-then-insert in both files,
  >   so scripts/ deterministically ends up at sys.path[0] regardless of
  >   what PYTHONPATH already put there.
  > - section-setup-assistant.sh's new #437 regression check (from the prior
  >   red commit) is now green; also tightened it to assert no AttributeError
  >   leaks (fixes a shellcheck SC2034 unused-var warning on the captured
  >   output).

- **feedback:** emit + route iteration feedback for AST-062 close (`11f810b`)
  > - 5 items: env-divergence incident (-> #439), suite-context replay ask (-> #440), recall-injection gap, reviewer-reproduces win, hotfix-stacking win

### Fixes
- **433:** mermaid diagrams pan and zoom instead of scrolling; audio player renders full-size on first paint (#433, #434) (`73865aa`)
  > - Mermaid graph view never scrolls: wheel/pinch zooms at the cursor
  >   (clamped), dragging pans, first render fits and centers the diagram
  > - A visible reset button (and double-click) re-fits the view; the
  >   detached window fills flexibly like the 3D viewers
  > - Audio players get an explicit minimum height so WebKit renders the
  >   full control strip on first paint instead of the compact pill
  > - Both verified live in Chrome before merge
  > 
  > Closes #433
  > Closes #434
- **red-first-preflight:** recognize __tests__/ dirs and .spec/.test files as test-only (`8146008`)
  > The classifier only matched (^|/)tests/, so a genuinely test-only RED
  > commit in a repo using __tests__/ directories or colocated *.spec.ts /
  > *.test.ts files was classified impl-touching and hard-blocked the move
  > to In review (false positive hit on hearthbase#155).
- **435:** suppress shellcheck SC2317 false positive in tmpdir-isolation section (`687dd86`)
  > - shellcheck 0.11.0 flags `return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0` at
  >   section-tmpdir-isolation.sh:49 as unreachable (SC2317), but it's the
  >   deliberate sourced-vs-executed dual-exit idiom: return succeeds when
  >   sourced, exit only runs when the file is executed directly.
  > - Add a targeted `# shellcheck disable=SC2317` with a comment explaining
  >   the idiom, so the gate's shellcheck step stops false-failing on main.

### Tests
- **437:** red -- setup.py's sys.path guard is shadowed by gate.sh's PYTHONPATH (`854eca0`)
  > - gate.sh exports PYTHONPATH=scripts/ before invoking setup.py. That puts
  >   scripts/ in sys.path at position 1, behind sys.path[0] (setup.py's own
  >   dir, scripts/assistant/) -- so the `if _SCRIPTS_DIR not in sys.path`
  >   guard sees it already present and skips the insert(0, ...) that's
  >   supposed to make scripts/ win.
  > - Without that, `import config as project_config` resolves
  >   scripts/assistant/config.py (the engine config module) instead of the
  >   intended scripts/config.py shared loader, and setup.py dies with an
  >   AttributeError -- this is #412's real root cause, deterministic under
  >   gate.sh's env.
  > - Add a regression check to section-setup-assistant.sh that runs scaffold
  >   with PYTHONPATH=scripts/ explicitly set (simulating gate.sh's env).
  >   Confirmed red: only the two new checks fail, the rest of the section
  >   passes.

### Performance
- **neural-view:** screen-space cluster culling for hover picks + voice-viz settings hoist (`b4b1fb5`)

  > intra-cluster links cull with their cluster, cross-cluster segments are

  > updateVisuals' rad = max note distance + r + 16. Voice viz reads the
  > settings snapshot once per frame instead of once per bar.

## v0.26.0 — 2026-07-21

### Features
- **neural-view:** voice visualizer panel + right-column layout + note media (#288) (`4d017c4`)
  > * docs(ui-options): voice visualizer decision rounds 1-3
  > 
  > Iterative UI mode artifacts for the neural-view voice panel: round 1
  > (four visualizer styles), round 2 (Mirror Spectrum variants with
  > IN/OUT/BOTH + direction colors), round 3 (Split Halves refinements,
  > chrome fixes). Human picked C1 Split Halves as final.
  > 
  > 
  > * feat(neural-view): voice panel with split-halves visualizer + right-column layout
  > 
  > Right column now splits voice panel (slim top), note inspect (middle,
  > absorbing freed space), activation log (bottom quarter, always filling
  > its bounds). One uniform sidebar width (--colw, the note panel's) across
  > left BRAINS bar, filters, talk, voice, inspect and log panels.
  > 
  > Voice panel: canvas split-halves visualizer (outbound cyan up / inbound
  > amber down, center-out frequency mapping, odd bar count, axis standoff),
  > pluggable audio sources via window.neuralVoice.setSource — MicSource
  > (getUserMedia + analyser, log-spaced voice-range bands, noise gate) and
  > SpeechSynthSource (native system TTS + synthesized envelope). Controls:
  > IN/OUT/BOTH direction (colored), mic mode dot (press-to-speak / always
  > on, Space to talk, Shift+Space toggles), cog settings panel replacing
  > the note slot (direction/mic duplicated in detail, echo guard, noise
  > suppression / shimmer / in-out feedback sliders, speech test phrases,
  > two-step reset). Echo guard ducks inbound while outbound speaks, on top
  > of stream echoCancellation. Panels below track the voice panel's live
  > footprint (open / folded / collapsed).
  > 
  > 
  > * feat(neural-view): detachable multi-note windows
  > 
  > Dragging the docked note's grip detaches it into its own fixed,
  > resizable window (snapshot content), freeing the sidebar slot — any
  > number of notes can stay open at once. ⌖ on a window re-attaches its
  > note to the sidebar (replacing whatever it shows), ✕ closes it;
  > wikilinks inside a window open in the sidebar. Replaces the old
  > custom-position drag of the single docked panel. Also: activation log
  > always fills its bottom quarter (folds to header), log sticky header
  > matches the panel translucency, note card and voice settings panel
  > mutually exclusive in the shared slot.
  > 
  > Closes #289 is tracked on the PR.
  > 
  > 
  > * feat(neural-view): note media — images, videos, 3D models, file links (#289)
  > 
  > render_body now tokenizes ![images](p) and [links](p) alongside
  > wikilinks; a new read-only /file/<repo>/<role>/<relpath> endpoint serves
  > brain-dir media behind an extension allowlist and traversal guards.
  > Client hydration: images inline (click opens a detached media-viewer
  > window with New tab / Download / in-page fullscreen), videos as inline
  > players, .glb/.gltf via vendored GLTFLoader (three r0.185.1, relative
  > imports rewritten same-dir, allowlisted + documented in vendor/README),
  > .obj/.stl via tiny hand parsers on core three — each as a live rotating
  > viewer that re-boots inside detached note windows. Remote http(s) image
  > URLs pass through untouched. ◎ on the note panel and detached windows
  > flies the 3D camera to the note's neuron. Note/settings panels also
  > reclaim the activation log's space when it is folded or collapsed
  > (--log-space mirrors --voice-below).
  > 
  > 
  > * feat(neural-view): pin sidebar note, header-drag windows, aspect-fit media viewer
  > 
  > 📌 pin on the docked note holds its slot: while pinned, a note that would
  > replace it opens directly as a detached window (staggered near the
  > sidebar); ⌖ re-attach passes force to take the slot back deliberately.
  > openNote refactored into renderNoteInto(root, ...) so notes render into
  > the docked panel or a fresh detached window alike. Detached windows now
  > drag by their whole header strip (role line/title, media bar) — buttons
  > still click through; the media viewer window sizes itself to the image's
  > aspect ratio on load (fit ≤70vw×80vh, never upscaled, nudged back
  > on-screen) so the full image is visible without cropping.
  > 
  > 
  > * feat(neural-view): media viewer polish — real downloads via /fetch proxy, in-image hover actions
  > 
  > Download fetches through a new same-origin /fetch proxy (remote hosts
  > rarely send CORS headers, so a client-side blob save was impossible):
  > http(s)-only, Referer must be this server's own page, size-capped and
  > timeout-bounded; new-tab fallback only if even the proxy fails. New tab
  > and Download move inside the image's top-right corner, revealed on
  > hovering that region; the window bar keeps name/⛶/⠿/✕ aligned on one
  > flex baseline with compact button text.
  > 
  > 
  > * style(neural-view): smaller in-image media action chips
  > 
  > 
  > * fix(neural-view): raise any window on click (capture phase), grip left of media name
  > 
  >

  > providers.sh (emits the AskUserQuestion option list) and
  > provider-dispatch.sh (execs the resolved script by provider id + stage,
  > degrading gracefully with a clear message when a provider is
  > registered but not yet backed by a script). Adding a provider is a
  > one-line registry edit -- no branching logic anywhere in this plugin
  > needs to change, proven by a fixture third-provider test.

  > v1 ships two entries: codex (available, routes to the existing
  > PRV-001..004 flow unchanged) and claude (registered, not yet
  > available -- its backend is CDX-054). SKILL.md's new first step asks
  > which provider to review with, always -- never auto-detected, since
  > which model is orchestrating this session doesn't determine which
  > model should review it; that's the whole point of /peer-review.
  > 
  > provider-dispatch.sh's row lookup went through one fix cycle: the
  > original IFS=$'\t' read-based parsing silently collapsed an empty
  > middle TSV column (bash treats tab as "IFS whitespace" even as the
  > sole IFS character), caught by a live codex self-review of the diff.
  > Replaced with a python3 lookup joined by \x1f (not IFS whitespace),
  > mirroring how providers.sh already parsed the same file correctly.

  > brain.py gains emit_event(root, obj), appending one \n-terminated JSON
  > line to <root>/.claude/brain-events.jsonl via a single os.write() to a
  > real O_APPEND file descriptor (os.open, not a buffered file object) --
  > concurrent appends of a whole line under PIPE_BUF are atomic on POSIX.

  > completes normally. Verified both by unit test and independently by the
  > reviewer forcing a real filesystem failure (an unwritable .claude path).
  > 
  > Concurrency stress-tested with real OS processes (not threads, which the
  > GIL would make a weak test): dev's own test at N=30, reviewer's
  > independent test at N=80/500-byte-padded lines -- zero interleaved or
  > lost lines in either.

  > (3d575e8) adds the implementation.

  > independently re-verified atomicity and non-blocking-failure with
  > separate fixtures, plus a higher-N concurrency test)

  > fixture which uses `$(cd "$BC" && ...)`. Since run-tests.sh sources every

  > marketplace/plugin CLI calls, identity fixtures all silently failed from a

  > identically regardless of host load) -- not the host-load flakiness
  > documented on #187/#208, an actual regression in this branch's own diff.

- **sw-101:** report 'unknown' when graphql reset is absent (#118) (`c3199ee`)
  > * test(sw-101, RED): _rate_limit_reset_human fallback reports core's reset as graphql's + leaks utcfromtimestamp DeprecationWarning
  > 
  > Real gh api rate_limit payload minus resources.graphql (derived from the
  > live rate-limit-endpoint-sample.json) fires the fallback branch, which reads
  > the top-level `rate` key -- an alias of resources.core whose reset is ~12min
  > later than graphql's. The QUEUED message then reports a wrong-but-confident
  > timestamp; the same python snippet also leaks a Python 3.13
  > datetime.utcfromtimestamp DeprecationWarning to stderr.
  > 
  > * fix(sw-101): report 'unknown' when graphql reset is absent + drop deprecated utcfromtimestamp
  > 
  > _rate_limit_reset_human() previously fell back to the top-level `rate` key
  > when resources.graphql was missing. In real gh api rate_limit responses `rate`
  > ALIASES resources.core, whose reset can differ from graphql's by ~12min, so the
  > fallback reported a wrong-but-confident timestamp in the 'rate-limited until X'
  > messages it feeds. Since the helper's job is the GRAPHQL reset (the counter that
  > masks GraphQL exhaustion), drop the fallback and report 'unknown' when graphql
  > is absent -- an honest unknown beats a confident-but-wrong time. Also switch
  > datetime.utcfromtimestamp (deprecated, Python 3.13) to timezone-aware
  > fromtimestamp so the helper stops leaking a DeprecationWarning to stderr.
  > 
  > The neural-view projects fake gh emitted a rate-only rate_limit payload (no
  > resources.graphql); update it to a realistic graphql-bearing shape with a
  > deliberately different `rate` reset so its reset-time test proves board.sh reads
  > graphql's reset, not the core alias. graphql.remaining is 0 only under the
  > rate-limit scenario so a plain gh failure isn't misclassified as a masked limit.
  > 
  > ---------
- **ui-options:** mockups must render in the target's real viewport at true scale (`d9678bf`)
  > A round-1 options page for a 466x466 round AMOLED sketched its mockups into
  > an arbitrary ~400px rounded rectangle, letting layouts look viable that the
  > real circular panel cannot fit. Step 1 now requires establishing the target's
  > actual resolution/shape first and using it as the mockup's buildable area
  > (true scale, real clipping, real scrolling).
- **build-next:** auto-merge requires fresh session consent, not config/memory alone (`eaab389`)
  > autoMerge:true was documented as itself being standing authorization to
  > bypass the self-approval permission check, and agents were citing a saved
  > memory note as a substitute for real consent. Both get rejected by the
  > permission classifier (correctly — a memory note is the agent granting
  > itself permission, and a config flag isn't a human message in the
  > transcript).
  > 
  > Add auto-review.md §0: ask once per session via AskUserQuestion before the
  > first autonomous merge attempt; the "yes" answer is scoped to that session
  > only and is deliberately never written back to memory as a standing grant.
- **prv004:** --model rejects a following flag as its value (#201 follow-up) (`d5fa1e4`)
  > --model in run.sh and peer-review.sh previously accepted ANY next token
  > as its value, including another flag -- e.g. `run.sh --model --staged`
  > silently set model="--staged" and swallowed --staged entirely, running
  > the review against the wrong diff with a bogus model slug. Caught by a
  > live codex self-review of the merged PRV-004 diff. Guard now requires
  > the value not start with "--"; reuses the existing missing-argument
  > error path, scoped strictly to --model.
- **neural-view:** restore horizontal padding on brain rows (`a50e47d`)
  > .sf-section label{padding:.15rem 0} (added for the top-level SEARCH IN
  > checkboxes) has higher specificity than .sf-brainrow{padding:.15rem .3rem}
  > — one class each, but the former also matches the `label` type selector —
  > so it silently zeroed every brain-row's horizontal padding. Scope it to
  > direct children only, which is all it was ever meant to reach.
- **sync-configs:** report real +added/-removed line counts in dry-run diff (#199) (`29202d3`)
  > The dry-run diff message said "would change (N lines)" where N was
  > the resulting file's total line count, not a diff size -- genuinely
  > misread once as a full-file-rewrite risk when it meant "results in an
  > N-line file" after a small insertion. Now computes actual added/
  > removed counts via difflib.ndiff and reports "(+N/-M lines)".
- **#197:** non-blocking stale-plugin-cache warning in preflight.sh (`ac01452`)
  > This repo dogfoods plugins/spec-workflow -- a session can invoke its
  > scripts either from this repo's own working tree (always current) or
  > via an installed marketplace cache copy that does not auto-update
  > when this repo's own source changes and merges. A real merge once
  > left the cache 77+ lines stale, causing a genuine correctness failure
  > (a newly-added identity role unresolvable via the cache path moments
  > after the merge that added it).
  > 
  > preflight.sh now compares 4 key files (identity_lib.py, identity.sh,
  > board.sh, config.py) between this repo's own scripts/ and the active
  > installed cache copy, printing one PLUGIN CACHE WARN line naming any
  > that diverge -- advisory only, never changes the script's exit code.
  > Silent no-op when this repo isn't spec-workflow's own source, or no
  > cache is found. Picks the active cache copy via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT
  > when set, else the newest by mtime -- not lexicographic sort order
  > (an earlier version of this fix used lexicographic-first-match, which
  > an independent reviewer caught as a real bug: on a machine with
  > multiple installed versions, it could silently compare against an
  > arbitrary, possibly long-dead cache directory instead of the one
  > actually in use).
  > 
  > Authored directly by the orchestrator, not a spawned dev agent --
  > this session hit repeated worktree-pinning/agent-identity resolution
  > failures under severe host load that made fresh dev-agent spawns
  > unreliable for this task; routed through two independent review
  > rounds before merge (the first round correctly caught an uncommitted
  > fix, branch staleness, and the version-selection bug above).
- **cdx005:** drop angle brackets from 6 skill descriptions (#177) (`dafb9bc`)
  > Codex's skill linter (quick_validate.py) rejects any SKILL.md
  > description containing a literal < or >. Fixes the 5 originally-scoped
  > offenders (ask-brain, ask-identity, create-inbound, find-task,
  > changelog-generate) plus a 6th found during the sweep
  > (peer-review/SKILL.md, merged with a violation since the task was
  > scoped): "review PR <n>" -> "review PR by number", and similar rewrites
  > for the other five, all preserving the slash command, argument concept,
  > and example trigger phrasing that made each original description precise.
  > 
  > Verified: quick_validate.py passes for all ~29 SKILL.md dirs across both
  > plugins (not just the 6 fixed), confirming no other latent violation.
  > 
  > TDD: red test (381cee7) loops the validator over every skill dir in both
  > plugins (not a hardcoded 6-item list, so it keeps catching regressions
  > in currently-good skills too) and proves the 6 known offenders fail
  > before the fix (4a9a870); skips gracefully if the external validator is
  > unavailable, matching the established pattern from CDX-003/004's tests.
- **refine-task-ui:** private repos need blob links, not raw.githubusercontent.com (`3ad944f`)
  > Caught live: a private repo's raw-content CDN 404s on the unauthenticated
  > image fetch an inline <img> tag makes, even though the URL looks
  > correct and the file is really there. Check repo visibility first and
  > branch the embed strategy accordingly.
- **refine-task-ui:** require linking the mockup source, not just screenshots (`e80645a`)
  > Caught live: a refined issue with only screenshots is incomplete —
  > screenshots freeze one moment, the mockup HTML is the actual artifact
  > (every option/round, live theme toggle, real markup an implementer can
  > diff against). Made this an explicit, checked requirement rather than
  > an implicit "cite the file" aside, with instructions for running it
  > live since GitHub's blob view only shows source, never executes it.
- **refine-task-ui:** drop angle brackets from SKILL.md description (#210) (#216) (`14aa926`)
  > Codex's skill linter (quick_validate.py) rejects any description containing
  > < or >. '/refine-task-ui <task-id>' tripped it; reworded to match the
  > existing '/find-task command with a search query' phrasing already used by
  > find-task and create-inbound's descriptions. Was failing
  > section-codex-skill-lint.sh's validator-exits-0/reports-valid checks
  > whenever the Codex skill validator is present locally, blocking a clean
  > full-suite gate for any in-flight task.
- **ui-options:** arm one-shot wake for hub answer instead of passive next-iteration poll (#218) (`34983c1`)
  > Closes #218
- **ui-mode:** cross-reference ui-options so Artifact never substitutes for the hub (`5228bf8`)
  > An agent session invoked /ui-mode, saw iterative UI mode was ON, then built
  > a UI-comparison page as a claude.ai Artifact instead of routing through
  > ui-options — the Artifact's #send can't POST back to ui-hub.py, so the
  > human's pick never reaches the agent, a dead end that looks fine until the
  > human tries to act on it.
  > 
  > ui-mode is a pure toggle/status skill and never said anything about
  > ui-options, so there was no cue connecting "mode is on" to "therefore use
  > ui-options, never Artifact" when a UI-options request arrived via ui-mode
  > rather than being named directly. Make that connection explicit.
- **mem004:** un-gitignore .claude/feedbacks/, commit feed + archive (#128) (`e4e96e8`)
  > Removes the single stale .gitignore line for .claude/feedbacks/ (the
  > local-state manifest already said track) and commits the existing
  > feed + archive files, per SPEC-MEMORY §6.5. Doc wording across
  > SPEC.md/SPEC-MEMORY.md/feedback SKILL.md was already consistent, no
  > edit needed. Adds a new repo-hygiene test asserting the live
  > git check-ignore fact so this can't silently regress.
  > 
  > Closes #128
- **cdx010:** stripfm() portability — replace sed line-range with awk+tail (`89b2945`)
  > The CI runner (GNU sed, Ubuntu) disagrees with BSD/macOS sed (this repo's
  > usual local dev environment) on whether a sed range address's end-regex
  > check applies on the range's own start line. Frontmatter's line 1 IS `---`,
  > so `1,/^---$/d` matches its own end-regex immediately on GNU sed, emptying
  > the whole body instead of stopping at the closing `---`. Every downstream
  > capability-language check that depended on stripfm()'s output cascaded to
  > FAIL on the actual CI run (41 assertions), while staying green locally
  > since local sed never hit the ambiguity. awk's line counter plus
  > `tail -n +N` have no start/end same-line ambiguity and behave identically
  > on GNU and BSD, so it replaces the sed range rather than patching around it.
- **237:** guard-brain-access.sh — technical enforcement of identity-brain isolation (`974e47e`)
  > CDX-031 gap #5: brains.md's brain-isolation design (subagents never see a
  > brain path) rested entirely on convention -- no technical boundary stopped a
  > direct read once a path was discovered. Adds a PreToolUse hook (Read + Bash
  > matchers) that blocks direct, raw content access to
  > .claude/identities/<role>/brain/** for every caller, orchestrator included,
  > funneling all legitimate access through brain.sh's own subcommands.
  > ROLE.md/DIRECTORY.md stay unblocked (read verbatim by design); Grep/Glob and
  > untargeted repo-wide sweeps are deliberately out of scope, documented in
  > docs/design/cdx-E3.md's #237 follow-up. HOOK-ONLY, Claude Code specific -- no
  > equivalent interception point exists under Codex.
  > 
  > Two review-round fixes folded in: an anchored regex that missed brain paths
  > embedded mid-token in python3/node one-liners, and a has_open substring gate
  > that missed pathlib.Path(...).read_text().

- neural-view: screen-space note picking, View-in-viewer button, clean board errors (`1f7a9ae`)
  > - Hover/click/dblclick note picking now projects note centers to screen
  >   pixels and picks the ball actually under the cursor, replacing the
  >   sprite-quad raycast that tooltipped halo quads' invisible margins while
  >   missing visible balls.
  > - First graph load with content always applies the camera fit: a stray
  >   wheel/drag during the initial /graph fetch no longer strands the view on
  >   the pre-data fallback framing.
  > - Clicking a note opens the inspect panel only; the panel gains a
  >   "View in Obsidian/VS Code/Terminal" button (GET /viewer reports which
  >   viewer POST /open would use; fixed fallback chain, settings later).
  > - board.sh list/item_id/fields gate on gh's exit code (capture-then-parse)
  >   instead of piping a failed read into json.load — no more JSONDecodeError
  >   tracebacks (ANSI-garbled) in the boards HUD; neural-view also classifies
  >   gh's misleading "unknown owner type" as the GraphQL rate-limit symptom
  >   it usually is.
- session-close: orchestrator charter (close protocol + default close-out format), session feedback document, mint last-action-is-delivery + session-close-protocol (`6ea2cad`)
- neural-view: all hover/click picking in screen space + ?hoverprobe self-check (`5113c0f`)
  > Synapse and repo-region hover still went through three.js raycasting and
  > kept producing hits that disagreed with the rendered pixels (tooltips over
  > empty space). Picking is now raycaster-free end to end: synapses pick by
  > point-to-projected-segment distance in CSS px, repo labels/regions by
  > projected label position and a thin band around the projected sphere rim
  > (interior still reads as empty space, #72). Notes keep the projected-ball
  > pick. A ?hoverprobe query flag overlays same-frame DOM rings/ticks at every
  > computed position — the alignment proof used to verify pick == pixels.
- neural-view: fix retina canvas sizing (the real offset bug) + hover ring (`f8c968f`)
  > canvas is a REPLACED element, so inset:0 alone never stretched it — with
  > renderer.setSize(..., false) not touching style, the element rendered at
  > its intrinsic buffer size (W*devicePixelRatio, 2x on retina) anchored
  > top-left, displacing the whole scene into the bottom-right corner while
  > pointer math correctly used viewport coordinates. That one missing
  > width/height:100% was the root cause of every "tooltips for things that
  > aren't there" / "first load in the corner" report on a retina display
  > (headless DPR=1 never reproduced it). Also adds a screen-space hover ring
  > around the hovered node, repositioned after each rendered frame.
- neural-view: collapsible/wider sidebar + per-brain colors from project.yaml (`4dff1b8`)
  > - Sidebar widens to 264px; BRAINS and BOARDS section headers toggle their
  >   sections (chevron state), and a ⟨ button slides the whole panel off-screen

  > - Each brain can declare its color at delegation.identities.<role>.color

- neural-view: labels live INSIDE their cluster + brain labels hover/click; dev = yellow (`f0684f0`)
  > Role and repo labels were offset a full cluster radius above their live

- neural-view: GraphQL budget discipline + activation log as right sidebar (`7dc02f0`)
  > Board reads share the user's 5000/hr GraphQL quota with the build loops and
  > were burning it around the clock: PROJECTS_TTL default rises 60->300s, the
  > page polls /projects every 60s (was 20), a rate-limited read opens a global
  > RATE_COOLDOWN circuit breaker (default 15min, env-tunable) so no repo
  > re-fetches while the quota is exhausted, and failures serve the last GOOD
  > data marked {stale, staleForSecs, staleReason} — the HUD shows "cached Nm
  > ago" instead of blanking a board it displayed seconds earlier.
  > 
  > The activation log moves from the bottom strip to a right sidebar with the
  > same collapse UX as the left panel (section header + slide-away tab,
  > persisted); it keeps 40 events now that it has vertical room, and the
  > inspect panel overlays it while open.

- neural-view: Talk deep-link panel, brain visibility toggle, loop badge (#105) (`b52068a`)
  > * neural-view: add Talk deep-link panel, brain visibility toggle, loop badge
  > 
  > - Talk button (left BRAINS bar) opens a panel to compose a claude-cli://open
  >   deep link (cwd + q, prefixed with /rename <project> <slug>) so a new
  >   session can be launched straight from the HUD with a short, greppable
  >   name. GET /graph now also returns `roots` (absolute path per repo) so the
  >   client can set `cwd` without depending on GitHub repo resolution.
  > - Per-brain eye toggle in the gauge list to temporarily hide a repo/role
  >   brain — hidden brains are excluded from the 3D scene, top-bar totals, and
  >   gauge sums, to help focus on a subset of brains. Persisted in localStorage.
  > - Best-effort "loop active" badge on repo labels/tooltips, from existing
  >   GET /sessions data (job state + name heuristic) — no real heartbeat yet,
  >   documented as approximate in-code.
  > - Minted an orchestrator brain note on the claude-cli:// deep-link pattern
  >   for future reuse.
  > 
  > * neural-view: fix BRAINS sidebar overflow, widen panel
  > 
  > The 264px gauges panel was tuned to exactly fit STR/SYN on one line before
  > the eyebtn existed (per the row's own comment) — adding it as a flex sibling
  > pushed long values (e.g. "SYN 739") past the edge. Move the eye toggle out
  > of flow (absolutely positioned in a reserved right-padding strip, revealed
  > on hover/focus/hidden) and widen #gauges from 264px to 296px for headroom;
  > the talk-panel anchor offset moves with it.
  > 
  > * neural-view: scope Talk to brains/identities via new ask-* skills, fix row layout
  > 
  > - Replace the single global "Talk" button with two scoped triggers: a small
  >   ✎ on each repo section header (whole-brain ask) and one on each identity
  >   row (that identity specifically) — talk is now always "to the brain" or
  >   "to an identity", never a bare/unscoped new session.
  > - Add ask-identity and ask-brain skills: read-only brain consults
  >   (/ask-identity <role> <question>, /ask-brain <question>) that ground an
  >   answer in recalled notes without running a build iteration or touching
  >   the board. The Talk panel composes `/rename <project> <slug>` + one of
  >   these two commands instead of a raw prompt.
  > - Fix BRAINS row layout: rname was flex:1, so a short role name still
  >   claimed all leftover width and shoved STR/SYN flush against the far
  >   edge; capped it instead so name/stats pack together. Action icons
  >   (ask + hide/show) moved into a reserved right-padding strip, revealed on
  >   hover/focus, so they never compete with STR/SYN for space.
  > 
  > * neural-view: cap force-sim explosion, trim/wrap activation log entries
  > 
  > - step(): a big brain (fab-cli/judge, ~570 notes) could "explode" on load —
  >   all nodes spawn in the same small ±130 cube regardless of final cluster,
  >   so with enough of them some pairs land nearly coincident by chance; the
  >   uncapped repulsion f=KREP/d2 turned that into a multi-million-unit force
  >   in one frame, launching nodes off past the camera faster than DAMP could
  >   tame it. Cap both the per-pair force and the resulting per-node speed.
  > - Activation log: drop the "+00:00" timezone suffix from each entry's
  >   timestamp (nobody was reading it) and stop ellipsis-truncating the
  >   note/link name — it's its own line now and wraps instead of cutting off
  >   mid-word ("inject deco…").
  > 
  > * neural-view: size notes by synapse count, tame hub-note flicker
  > 
  > fab-cli/judge's glossary-index (594 links) and keywords-index (383 links)
  > are real hubs — dozens of other notes [[wikilink]] to them — but were sized
  > like any ordinary 1-10-link note, and every one of those springs pulled on
  > them at full strength every frame, so they never settled (the "two notes
  > flickering" behind the starburst render).
  > 
  > - Node radius now also grows with sqrt(degree) (capped), so a genuine hub
  >   reads as one visually instead of being buried at default size.
  > - Each spring's pull is now split by 1/sqrt(degree) per endpoint, so a
  >   node's total incoming spring force scales with sqrt(degree) instead of
  >   degree — ordinary notes are unaffected, hub notes stop oscillating.
  > 
  > * neural-view: put /ask-* first, /rename last in Talk deep links
  > 
  > Confirmed by manual testing: the harness only recognizes a slash command on
  > the first line of a multi-line pre-filled prompt. /rename-first silently ate
  > the /ask-identity or /ask-brain instruction — only the rename ever fired.
  > Swap the order so the real instruction runs and /rename, now trailing on
  > its own line, still gets picked up and acted on afterward. Updated the
  > orchestrator brain note on the deep-link pattern with this confirmed
  > finding (previously flagged as unverified).
  > 
  > * neural-view: extra damping for high-degree notes so hubs settle too
  > 
  > The sqrt(degree) spring normalization stopped hub notes from exploding, but
  > they still net ~sqrt(degree)x an ordinary note's force every frame — mostly
  > from hundreds of neighbors' own small settling motions, which never fully
  > stop. That read as gentle persistent jitter instead of coming to rest like
  > every other note. Added degree-scaled extra damping (no-op below ~9 links,
  > so ordinary notes are unaffected) to bleed that off faster.
  > 
  > * neural-view: namespace ask-identity/ask-brain as /spec-workflow:*
  > 
  > Plugin skills are always invoked namespaced ("/plugin-name:skill-name"),
  > never bare — confirmed by the user hitting "Unknown command: /ask-identity"
  > when clicking a generated Talk deep link. The bare names in buildTalkText()
  > and both SKILL.md descriptions were simply wrong regardless of the
  > first-line-vs-multiline ordering fix from the previous commit. Recorded
  > this (plus the separate installed-plugin-version-pin gotcha the user also
  > hit) in the orchestrator brain note.
  > 
  > * retro: triage pending feedback (5 items), mint 2 new orchestrator notes
  > 
  > - brain-note x3: bumped claude-cli-deep-links-pattern (feedback item 0,
  >   same lesson already captured in-session); minted
  >   live-redeploy-screenshot-loop-for-visual-features and
  >   permission-classifier-blocks-self-merge-drafts.
  > - backlog x2: #106 (skill-authoring guidance should state namespacing),
  >   #107 (no convention for previewing a worktree branch against a live
  >   local process).
  > - Cold retro (no live dev/reviewer subagents this session) — worked from
  >   the recorded feedback record's text, no interview.

- neural-view: spatial-grid repulsion + settle-freeze — same physics, no more O(n²) every frame (`9719bc5`)
  > Large brains (fab-cli/card-vault: ~5k notes, ~10k synapses) dropped the viz
  > to slideshow FPS: step() computed all-pairs repulsion (~17M iterations/frame
  > at 5.9k nodes) on every animation frame, forever, even at rest.
  > 
  > Three changes, none visible:
  > - repulsion now runs on a uniform spatial hash grid sized to the existing
  >   300-unit cutoff (13 forward-neighbor offsets = each pair once). Identical
  >   forces to the all-pairs loop — verified by harness, max velocity diff 1e-14
  >   (float summation order) — at 2-5x the speed, and no longer O(n²) in the
  >   spread-out settled state.
  > - settle-freeze: after ~1.5s of sustained sub-threshold average speed the
  >   integrator sleeps (hl decay, pulses, hover, camera all keep running).
  >   applyGraph() calls wakeSim() on every reload/re-filter/brain toggle, so
  >   anything that can move nodes resumes integration. A settled static corpus
  >   costs ~zero sim time.
  > - spawn cube scales with cbrt(node count): constant initial density instead
  >   of thousands of notes packed inside everyone's cutoff (the grid's worst
  >   case and a first-frame shockwave). Same look, cheap settle at any size.
  > 
  > neural-view test sections: same 10 pre-existing env failures before and
  > after; no new failures.

- neural-view: fix results-panel overlap, shrink search bar, stop unnecessary sim wake (#112) (`9dc7a96`)
  > * neural-view: fix search results overlapping the bar, shrink search bar width
  > 
  > - #search-results never overrode the base .hud{position:fixed}, so instead
  >   of stacking in normal flow below #searchbar inside #search-wrap's flex
  >   column, it broke out to its own fixed position — rendering as a near-
  >   full-width overlay ON TOP of the bar (and the side panels) instead of
  >   attached below it. Explicit position:static fixes it.
  > - #search-wrap was min(1040px,84vw) — wide enough to overlap the BRAINS
  >   and activation-log side panels on common viewport widths. Shrunk to
  >   min(600px,52vw).
  > 
  > * neural-view: only wakeSim() when the visible note set actually changes
  > 
  > applyGraph() called wakeSim() unconditionally on every 15s graph poll, even
  > when nothing changed — existing notes keep their settled x/y/z (old.x
  > reuse), so there was nothing for that wake to accomplish on a no-op
  > reload. At the thousands-of-notes scale this now runs at, that cost twice
  > over: (1) a real perf hit, a full physics burst every single poll forever;
  > (2) each unnecessary wake gave repulsion (strong at close range) another
  > chance to nudge notes apart before the much weaker cluster gravity could
  > fully pull them back within the ~1.5s settle-freeze window, and refreezing
  > there — repeated over a long-running session, this is what dispersed a
  > brain that used to sit in a tight cluster. Gate the wake on the visible
  > note-id set actually differing (added/removed/hide-toggle) instead.
  > 
  > A currently-already-dispersed tab needs a fresh page load to re-settle
  > cleanly (nodes re-spawn and converge once, uninterrupted, since polling can
  > no longer perturb them) — this fix stops it from happening again, it
  > doesn't retroactively re-tighten an already-open tab's live state.
- neural-view: merge scale/perf rewrite (neural-view-perf) with the results panel (#113) (`fe7999d`)
  > * neural-view: scale physics to card-vault-size brains without changing the look
  > 
  > fab-cli/card-vault (~5k notes / ~10k synapses) dropped the viz to slideshow
  > FPS: step() ran all-pairs repulsion (~17M iterations) on every rendered
  > frame, and — because the sim has no dt term — that lag was also silently
  > setting the motion speed big graphs settled at.
  > 
  > - repulsion runs on a uniform spatial hash grid sized to the existing
  >   300-unit cutoff: same pairs, same forces (harness-verified, max velocity
  >   diff ~1e-14), no O(n²) scan. The original all-pairs loop is kept as the
  >   calibration path.
  > - sim pacing self-calibrates: when the node count changes >10%, one step
  >   runs the original all-pairs code and its measured duration becomes the
  >   step interval — big graphs advance at the same wall-clock rate the old
  >   code produced on this machine; small graphs step at 60Hz as always.
  >   Calibration never fires while a pointer is dragging (the 60-100ms hitch
  >   read as the rotation freezing).
  > - fresh nodes spawn inside their own cluster's region at ~resting density
  >   instead of piled into a ±130 cube at the origin — kills the reload
  >   'explosion' (thousands of coincident nodes rocketing outward at the
  >   pair-force cap, then crawling back), and with it the stretched-line phase
  >   while settling.
  > - big fresh spawns fast-forward up to 300 sim steps within an 8ms/frame
  >   budget: same trajectory, the user just doesn't watch it in real time.
  > - non-finite node state self-heals (re-seat at cluster center): one NaN
  >   position poisons three.js bounding spheres and whole buffers vanish —
  >   'content disappeared'.
  > - status chip shows a live FPS counter (was the static 'recalls light up'
  >   tagline); reduced-motion/3D-unavailable cases preserved.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.3: batched rendering, adaptive resolution, version tag, ?perf timers
  > 
  > - neurons (core+halo) render as two instanced billboard layers, all synapse
  >   lines as ONE LineSegments, ambient pulses as one instanced layer: ~25k
  >   draw calls -> 4 at card-vault scale. Same textures, additive blending,
  >   and per-note/per-link formulas — billboarding replicated in the vertex
  >   shader (THREE.Sprite math), FogExp2 replicated in the fragment shader,
  >   per-link opacity encoded as vertex-color scale (equivalent under additive
  >   blending). Hover/click/tooltips were already screen-space projections, so
  >   interaction is untouched.
  > - adaptive resolution governor: render DPR steps down 0.25 while fps < 45
  >   and restores after 3 healthy seconds — fill rate (retina DPR-2 + 4x MSAA
  >   x additive halo overdraw) is the remaining bottleneck at scale.
  > - status chip: NV_VERSION template version tag (which build is this tab
  >   rendering — three copies of this file exist on disk) + live fps + ?perf
  >   per-section timers (sim/vis/draw EMAs).
  > - template marker tests updated to the batched implementation's markers.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.4: status-chip segments explain themselves on hover
  > 
  > 'live', the version tag, fps, the adaptive-resolution marker, the ?perf
  > timers and the reduced-motion note each carry a native title tooltip
  > saying what the readout means.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.5: perf timers toggleable from Settings (?perf forces on)
  > 
  > ⚙ Settings gains 'Show performance timers', persisted in uiState; the
  > ?perf URL flag still force-enables them for a session (checkbox shown
  > checked+disabled). Chip tooltips explain each timer.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.6: tabs report live metrics; status prints them
  > 
  > Each open tab POSTs {version, fps, dpr, sim/vis/draw ms, notes, links} to
  > /metrics about once a second; GET /metrics returns the recent clients and
  > `neural-view.py status` prints one viewer line per tab — an agent (or a
  > human in a terminal) can now measure the page's real frame rate without
  > screenshots. Entries expire after 30s.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.7: conservative settle-freeze + spd/asleep in metrics
  > 
  > Headless measurement showed the physics step dominating frame time
  > (sim 20.7ms of a 30ms frame at 6.1k notes) with the sim running forever.
  > Settle-freeze returns WITHOUT force cooling (which distorted final layout):
  > integrate until avg per-node speed stays under 0.05 for 240 steps, then
  > sleep; wakeSim() on every applyGraph. Average speed + asleep state are
  > exported in /metrics to tune the threshold from data.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.8: calm threshold 0.12 — measured jitter floor is ~0.08
  > 
  > spd metric showed settled avg speed asymptoting at 0.076-0.087, above the
  > 0.05 threshold, so the freeze never engaged. 0.12 with 240 sustained calm
  > steps freezes only truly-settled scenes (~2-3 units/s drift).
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.9: freeze actually engages, bounded steps at extreme scale
  > 
  > - wakeSim() only on real topology change (fresh nodes / count change) — the
  >   unconditional wake on every 15s graph poll reset the calm counter forever,
  >   so the settle-freeze never fired. Calm window shortened to 120 steps.
  > - self-tuning duty cycle for grid repulsion: when a measured step exceeds
  >   ~40ms, each step processes 1/P of the cells with per-pair force scaled by
  >   P (mean force unchanged, per-impulse cap still binds); P halves when steps
  >   get cheap and stays 1 (exact physics) for anything that fits the budget —
  >   measured 1.8s/step at a 60k-note synthetic scene, fps 0.
  > - fast-forward burst bails after any single step over 24ms.
  > - simPhaseP exported as  in /metrics.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.10: scale-adaptive layout, camera and fog
  > 
  > A brain of n notes settles into a ball of radius ~55·cbrt(n); the layout now
  > spaces role clusters and sizes repo regions by those radii instead of packing
  > everything into a fixed ~110-unit region. At 10k-note brains the old layout
  > kept tens of thousands of nodes permanently inside each other's repulsion
  > cutoff — an equilibrium so dense the sim could neither be cheap nor settle
  > (measured: 550-700ms/step even at P=64 duty cycle). Constant equilibrium
  > density makes grid cells bounded at any corpus size. Camera far plane, zoom
  > ceiling and fog density now track the scene's physical radius so big scenes
  > aren't clipped or fogged to black. Small scenes land within a few units of
  > the old layout.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.11: settle actually completes at scale
  > 
  > Three fixes from measured 10x behavior (52-60fps but spd pinned at 16-22,
  > P at 32-64, never sleeping):
  > - duty-cycled steps apply UNSCALED forces: scaling by P into the per-impulse
  >   cap made bang-bang dynamics that never calmed. Unscaled = P× slower
  >   relaxation toward the SAME equilibrium.
  > - the spatial grid is cached and rebuilt every 8 steps — per-step Map churn
  >   alone was ~15-25ms at 60k nodes, pinning the duty cycle high.
  > - historical-cadence calibration only below 20k notes; big scenes pace by
  >   their own measured step cost (interval = 1.6x step, capped 200ms) instead
  >   of one violent step every few seconds.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.12: sampled per-block repulsion — no starvation, bounded work
  > 
  > Duty-cycling starved repulsion (springs/gravity fire every step, each
  > cell's repulsion once per P): the layout compressed and oscillated around a
  > too-dense equilibrium — measured spd pinned 11-19, P at 32-64, never
  > sleeping. Replaced with per-cell-block SAMPLING: every block processed every
  > step; oversized blocks iterate rows with a stride and scale each sampled
  > pair by it (mean-preserving; per-impulse cap intact). Stride is 1 (exact
  > physics) at target density; sampling only engages in dense transients.
  > p in /metrics now reports the max stride.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.13: cap spring force — unsatisfiable link topologies settle softly
  > 
  > Measured on a 60k synthetic corpus with long-range links: unbounded spring
  > pull (~10 units/step across a big ball) compressed clusters to ~9x target
  > density and the sim thrashed forever (spd ~21, stride ~55). Forces near
  > target length are far below the +/-3 cap, so settled scenes are unaffected.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.14: scale cluster gravity for constant equilibrium density
  > 
  > With constant gravity a ball's equilibrium radius goes as N^(1/4) — density
  > grows with note count. At 10k-note brains that meant ~300 nodes per grid
  > cell, repulsion sampling strides ~50, and sampling variance acting as a
  > permanent noise floor (spd pinned ~20 across every sampling scheme tried;
  > the scene never slept). Gravity scaled by cbrt(600/n) pins equilibrium
  > density to the small-brain value, making neighbor counts, step cost, and
  > settling corpus-size-independent. Brains under 600 notes unchanged; big
  > brains' balls now actually match the cbrt(n) radius the layout and spawn
  > already assume.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.15: container gravity for big brains — density capped by construction
  > 
  > Center-pull gravity puts equilibrium density at N^(1/4)-and-worse (force
  > caps saturate repulsion pressure, so even scaled pulls over-compress:
  > measured 4.5x target density, strides ~15, spd noise floor ~9). Big brains
  > (>600 notes) now get a CONTAINER instead: zero gravity inside ballR(n),
  > spring-to-shell beyond — density cannot exceed target at any corpus size,
  > no calibration constant. Small brains keep the classic center pull
  > unchanged.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.16: calm threshold 0.2 — settle tails measured stalling at 0.10-0.15
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.17: per-note visuals on the GPU — CPU vis cost only when something changed
  > 
  > Per-note formulas (throb, recall highlight, hover, search, graduated dim)
  > move into the note layers' vertex shader, driven by uTick/uHoverIdx/
  > uSearchOn uniforms and mostly-static instance attributes. Ambient pulse
  > dots ride their links entirely in-shader (endpoints as attributes, uNow
  > drives the drift). The CPU now uploads:
  > - positions (notes / line endpoints / pulse endpoints): stepped frames only
  > - aHl: only notes with a fading recall highlight (sparse set)
  > - aSearch + link colors + pulse dim: on search/hover-link changes only
  > The O(n) live-centroid pass for labels/regions is gated to stepped frames.
  > At 60k notes the always-on vis loop was 12-18ms/frame — now ~0 between
  > steps and when asleep. Marker tests updated.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.18: graph pipeline survives huge corpora
  > 
  > Measured at 180k notes: /graph took 39s to scan and produced an 86MB
  > payload — with the fixed 15s poll, the server never stopped scanning and
  > every tab re-parsed 86MB continuously.
  > - server: /graph payload cached with a TTL of 6x its own measured build
  >   cost (floor 15s), so overlapping polls serve bytes instead of re-scanning.
  > - client: poll interval stretches to 8x the measured load time (floor 15s).
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.19: settle-phase pacing keeps huge scenes interactive
  > 
  > At 180k notes a full step is ~150ms and the 200ms interval cap meant 2fps
  > until the freeze. Progress-paced scenes now step at 4x their own measured
  > step cost (sim ≤ ~1/4 wall-clock): the page stays interactive while
  > organizing; settling takes proportionally longer and the freeze ends it.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.25.20: wall-clock calm criterion + cancel fast-forward on heavy steps
  > 
  > - fast-forward cancels when a single step exceeds ~80ms: one heavy step per
  >   frame rendered the whole 300-step burst at 2fps on a 180k scene.
  > - sleep is judged on perceived drift (spd x steps/sec < 3 units/s, with an
  >   absolute spd<3 sanity guard): progress-paced scenes step rarely, so the
  >   per-step threshold made a 180k scene decay an exponential tail for ~15min
  >   after its motion was already invisible.
  > 
  > 
  > * neural-view v0.26.0: the scale/performance increment ships
  > 
  > Measured end state (headless probe, /metrics):
  > - 1x (6.1k notes):    126 fps · asleep · sim 0 · vis 0   (was 3 fps, never settled)
  > - 10x (60k notes):    120 fps · asleep · settles in ~25s (was 0 fps)
  > - 30x (180k notes):   121 fps · asleep · 58-124 fps THROUGHOUT the settle
  > Draw calls ~25k -> 4; physics exact (stride 1) at every measured scale;
  > sim+vis cost ~0 at rest; graph pipeline TTL-cached and adaptively polled.
  > 
  > 
  > * retro: mint 5 orchestrator notes from the neural-view perf session
  > 
  > ui-perf-metrics-loop, synthetic-corpus-perf-rig, dev-server-port-contention,
  > plugin-edits-canonical-repo-branch, feedback-feed-yaml-quoting. Feed routing
  > is local-only here (.claude/feedbacks gitignored by this repo's convention).

- neural-view: fix constellation spacing, clickable activation log, frontmatter/full-text search (#114) (`a051a22`)
  > * neural-view: fix constellation spacing blowout, make activation log clickable
  > 
  > - layoutClusters(): repo constellation spacing was sized off the SUM of
  >   every repo's radius, which let one outsized brain (fab-cli/card-vault at
  >   5,924 notes vs. 15-125 in every other repo — a >45x ratio) blow the whole
  >   layout out, dragging every small repo far apart from every OTHER small
  >   repo too, not just from the giant one. Now sized off the MEDIAN repo
  >   radius (keeps the typical case tight); any repo substantially bigger than
  >   that gets pushed further out along its own already-assigned fibSphere
  >   direction individually, instead of inflating everyone's spacing.
  > - Activation log entries that name a single note (seed/hop/inject — not a
  >   consult, whose target is a link key "a->b", not one slug) are now
  >   clickable/Enter-able: flies the camera to that note and opens the same
  >   detail panel a search-result row does.
  > 
  > * neural-view: search frontmatter + full text, with per-scope toggles
  > 
  > - /graph nodes now also carry `paths`/`source` (frontmatter fields already
  >   parsed for tags/strength — cheap to include, unlike the note BODY).
  > - New GET /search-body?q=<query>: server-side substring scan across every
  >   note's body text, TTL-cached like /graph, returns matching ids only —
  >   body text itself is never shipped to the client (payload-size reasons at
  >   thousands-of-notes scale, same rationale as /graph).
  > - Filters popover gains two more "Search in" scopes: Frontmatter (paths +
  >   source) and Full text (note body, via the new endpoint — async, so
  >   triggerSearch()/refreshSearchHighlight() now await it before computing
  >   matches, with a stale-response guard in case a newer search/clear lands
  >   first).
  > 
  > * neural-view: apply the same median-radius packing to role clusters within a repo
  > 
  > The constellation-spacing fix only applied one level up (repos within the
  > scene) — the exact same failure mode existed one level down: role clusters
  > within a single repo were spaced by ring = maxBall*1.7 (the LARGEST role's
  > ball), so a repo with one huge role (fab-cli/card-vault at 5,051 notes) and
  > several small ones (judge 595, player 267, orchestrator 11) scattered the
  > small roles across a sphere sized for the giant one — each ending up in its
  > own isolated bubble far from the others, when only card-vault actually
  > needed that much room. That's what "the identities within a brain don't
  > look like a single entity anymore" was.
  > 
  > Factored the median-radius-with-outlier-pushout logic (previously inline
  > for the repo constellation) into a shared packByRadius() helper, and
  > applied it to role-cluster placement too. Also fixes a latent sizing bug
  > this surfaced: the repo's own bounding radius (used for its wireframe
  > region AND for the outer constellation spacing) was computed as
  > "ring + maxBall", which assumed every role sat at exactly `ring` — never
  > true once an outlier gets pushed further out. Now computed from each role's
  > ACTUAL final offset (post-pushout) + its own ball radius.
  > 
  > * neural-view: bump NV_VERSION to 0.27.0
  > 
  > Per the version's own comment ("bump the MINOR when the increment ships"),
  > which I hadn't been doing across the last several commits (constellation
  > spacing fix, clickable activation log, frontmatter/full-text search, role-
  > cluster packing fix) — the human was correctly suspicious that the topbar
  > still read v0.26.0 through all of that, since that string is the one real
  > signal for "is this tab actually running what I think it is."
  > 
  > * neural-view: tighten role-cluster ring so siblings merge like brain lobes
  > 
  > Confirmed by an old-vs-new side-by-side comparison on development-skills
  > (same repo, same 3 roles, same relative arrangement in both) — the ring
  > multiplier (1.7x the typical role's own ball radius) kept same-sized role
  > clusters clearly apart from each other, reading as three separate glowing
  > balls sitting inside a shared wireframe container. The OLD layout read as
  > one brain with lobes because its role-cluster ring was proportionally much
  > tighter relative to each cluster's own size.
  > 
  > Dropped the multiplier to 0.55 — smaller than a typical role's own ball
  > radius, so similarly-sized siblings now overlap/merge into one shape
  > instead of floating apart. The outlier push-out (role substantially bigger
  > than the typical sibling, e.g. fab-cli/card-vault) is unaffected: it still
  > computes its extra distance from the (now smaller) typical baseline, so a
  > genuinely huge role still gets its own room without dragging its tiny
  > siblings along the way the pre-fix formula did.
  > 
  > Also bumps NV_VERSION 0.27.0 -> 0.27.1 per its own "bump on every change"
  > convention.

- board-queue: fix durability of crashed flush + add lockdir liveness probe (#121) (`dd1c089`)
  > * fix(board): restore #78 item-id cache + list auto-flush lost by e0df2a9
  > 
  > e0df2a9 ("chore: .neural-network, settings.json, board.sh") rewrote
  > item_id/list/fields to a capture-then-parse pattern but was based on a
  > pre-#78 copy of board.sh, silently deleting CACHE_FILE/_cache_get and
  > list's auto-flush + rate-limit-branched failure message while leaving
  > board-queue.sh's _item_id_rl/_mutate_field/_cache_put/_cache_drop still
  > calling _cache_get/$CACHE_FILE. Every flush broke with "_cache_get:
  > command not found" / "CACHE_FILE: unbound variable" on stderr, and
  > `list` stopped auto-flushing the queue and lost its RATE-LIMITED
  > message. Discovered while building the #104 durability fix, whose new
  > tests exercise flush/_item_id_rl directly. Prerequisite for #104, not
  > part of its scope.
  > 
  > * test(104): failing tests for board-queue durability + lock liveness (red)
  > 
  > Live incident 2026-07-08: a flush crashed mid-replay leaving neither the
  > queue file nor an aside file behind -- every queued mutation had to be
  > reconstructed by hand. Adds:
  > 
  > - (v) crash after the aside-move but before the first apply: every
  >   originally-queued entry must survive on disk and remain recoverable.
  > - (w) crash after the last apply but before the aside file's final
  >   cleanup: no duplicate application, nothing stuck.
  > - (x) a REAL (non-rate-limit) apply failure must not silently vanish
  >   the entry -- it must survive in the live queue file, and the flush
  >   must keep processing the other lines in the batch. Needs a new fake-gh
  >   trigger, FAKE_GH_EDIT_REAL_FAIL_ON, for a one-off non-rate-limited
  >   item-edit failure.
  > - (y) a lockdir whose pidfile names a definitively-dead PID is broken
  >   immediately, without waiting out the TTL.
  > - (z) a lockdir whose pidfile names a live PID is left alone (existing
  >   SKIP behavior preserved).
  > 
  > All five currently fail against board-queue.sh's current
  > _flush_queue_locked (unconditional aside rm, dropped rc=1 entries) and
  > _queue_lock_acquire (TTL-only, no liveness probe) -- implementation
  > follows in the next commits.
  > 
  > * test(104): fix harness bugs found while driving the durability tests
  > 
  > Two bugs in the (v)/(w)/(x) tests written in the previous commit,
  > found while implementing against them:
  > 
  > - (v)/(x) queued two DIFFERENT issue numbers, but the fixture fake gh's
  >   item-list only ever makes ONE issue# (FAKE_GH_ISSUE_NUM) visible --
  >   the second issue# could never resolve regardless of durability.
  >   Switched both to the SAME issue# with two different op kinds (so
  >   #92's dedupe doesn't collapse them), matching the existing (b)/(d)
  >   pattern.
  > - (w) waited on the wrong _flush_sync tag ("<tag>-done"'s ready file)
  >   without ever releasing the FIRST sync point ("<tag>"), so the flush
  >   process sat parked at the pre-apply pause (test (v)'s window) until
  >   its own internal wait cap gave up -- never reaching the crash point
  >   the test intended. Now releases the first sync point immediately
  >   before waiting on the second.
  > 
  > * feat(104): board-queue durability -- per-entry aside bookkeeping + dead-lock liveness probe
  > 
  > Live incident 2026-07-08 ~13:14-13:19Z: a flush took the lockdir, died
  > mid-replay, and left NEITHER the queue file NOR an aside file behind --
  > every queued mutation had to be reconstructed by hand from session
  > memory. Two fixes:
  > 
  > 1. Durability (_flush_queue_locked): the aside file used to be
  >    unconditionally `rm -f`'d once the replay loop finished, regardless
  >    of whether every line had actually been confirmed applied -- a
  >    kill -9 anywhere in the loop could lose everything not yet requeued.
  >    Now rewritten (via the new _aside_write_remaining helper) after
  >    EVERY line is resolved -- applied, requeued on rate limit, or
  >    written back on a real failure -- so it always holds exactly
  >    "remaining unconfirmed work". A crash at any point leaves every
  >    not-yet-confirmed entry either still in the aside file or already
  >    durably in $QUEUE_FILE, never in neither. Also: a real (non-rate-
  >    limit, rc=1) apply failure used to vanish the line silently -- only
  >    rc==2 (rate-limited) got written back anywhere. Now rc==1 writes the
  >    line back to $QUEUE_FILE too (so a human/next flush can see and
  >    address it) instead of dropping it, and the loop keeps processing
  >    the OTHER lines in the batch (unlike rc==2, which stops touching gh
  >    entirely once tripped).
  > 
  > 2. Liveness probe (_queue_lock_acquire/_queue_lock_release): a stale-
  >    but-under-TTL lock with no live holder used to sit SKIPping every
  >    auto-flush for up to the full TTL (600s default) before a human
  >    diagnosed and rmdir'd it by hand. Every acquired lock now also
  >    writes a pidfile ($QUEUE_LOCK_DIR/pid, $$). When mkdir fails, the
  >    pidfile is checked FIRST via `kill -0`: a definitively-dead holder
  >    breaks the lock immediately, regardless of TTL age. A live holder,
  >    or no pidfile (a lock from a pre-#104 build), falls back to the
  >    existing TTL-age behavior unchanged.
  > 
  > Closes #104.
  > 
  > * docs(104): document the lock liveness probe + replay durability guarantee
  > 
  > SPEC.md has no board-queue-internals section to delta (verified: no
  > "board-queue"/"flush"/lockdir mentions there at all) -- this is an
  > ad-hoc hardening fix, not part of a numbered spec epic, so the only
  > user-facing doc surface is this README paragraph.
  > 
  > * test(104): failing test for _aside_write_remaining non-atomicity (red)
  > 
  > Review finding on PR #121: the first cut of _aside_write_remaining
  > truncated the aside file in place (`: >"$file"` then appended line-by-
  > line) -- a kill -9 between the truncate and the last append leaves the
  > aside file empty or partially written, i.e. an entry mid-rewrite in
  > NEITHER the aside file nor $QUEUE_FILE. That's exactly the "entry
  > exists in neither location" invariant #104 exists to close, just
  > relocated from the old unconditional `rm -f` to this per-entry
  > rewrite -- on the hot path (every replay with >=1 entry pending), not
  > a corner case.
  > 
  > Adds (aa), gated behind a new BOARD_QUEUE_TEST_ASIDE_SYNC=1 opt-in
  > (separate from the general BOARD_QUEUE_TEST_SYNC gate _flush_sync
  > itself checks, since this pause point fires once per queued line, not
  > once per flush -- an unconditional pause here would cost every OTHER
  > sync-using test above (v/w/x/m/n/r/s) up to
  > BOARD_QUEUE_TEST_SYNC_MAX_WAIT_ITERS' worth of wall-clock time per
  > line). Currently fails: the old code has no such sync point at all, so
  > the test's pause never fires and the aside file is already gone
  > (unconditionally rm -f'd) by the time the assertions run.
  > 
  > * fix(104): make _aside_write_remaining's rewrite of the aside file atomic
  > 
  > Review finding on PR #121 (blocking): the aside file's rewrite itself
  > wasn't atomic -- it truncated in place then appended line-by-line, so a
  > kill -9 mid-write could leave it empty or partially written, i.e. an
  > entry mid-rewrite in neither the aside file nor $QUEUE_FILE. Fixed by
  > writing the new content to a sibling temp file first, then a single
  > atomic `mv` over the aside path -- the same mv-based atomicity
  > _flush_queue_locked already relies on for the queue file itself,
  > applied here too: the aside path always shows either its full old
  > content or its full new content, never a partial write.
  > 
  > Adds the BOARD_QUEUE_TEST_ASIDE_SYNC=1 opt-in sync point the previous
  > test commit exercises, gated separately from the general
  > BOARD_QUEUE_TEST_SYNC check so it costs nothing for every other
  > sync-using test in this file.
  >

- neural-view: render GFM pipe tables + italic in HUD sidebar notes (#120) (`bead76d`)
  > * test(117, RED): render_body has no GFM pipe-table support
  > 
  > render_body() falls through to a single <p> wrapping raw pipe-table
  > text for any block it doesn't recognize as a heading or bullet list,
  > and inline() has no italic (*text*/_text_) support. Add a section test
  > that renders a fixture note body containing a pipe table, a header,
  > bold, and italic text, asserting on real <table>/<thead>/<tbody>/<th>/
  > <td> markup and <em> output -- currently RED (8 failing checks).
  > 
  > * feat(117): render GFM pipe tables and italic in HUD sidebar notes
  > 
  > render_body() now detects a pipe-table block (header row + a
  > :---/---: separator row, GFM-style) and emits real <table><thead>
  > <tbody> markup instead of falling through to a raw <p>. inline() gains
  > *text*/_text_ -> <em> support, applied after **bold** so a "**" pair
  > can't be misread as two italic markers. Table cells run through
  > inline() too, so bold/italic/code/wikilinks inside a cell still work.

- neural-view: schema-driven facet filter panel (numeric + enum tri-state) (`3057cbf`)
  > Adds a per-brain filter UI driven by an optional SCHEMA.json a brain's
  > generator can declare (fab-cli's build-card-vault.py is the reference
  > producer) — shown only when exactly one schema-having brain is the sole
  > BRAINS selection:
  > 
  > - Numeric facets (cost/power/defense/...): operator (=/>/</>=/<=) + value,
  >   matched against /graph's per-node `num` field (any per-variant value, e.g.
  >   a merged pitch-variant card's power-red/yellow/blue, satisfies via OR).
  > - Enum facets (type/subtype/class/talent/rarity/interacts-with): tri-state
  >   rows (unselected -> include -> exclude -> unselected) instead of plain
  >   checkboxes, so exclusion no longer requires typing "-field:value" by hand.
  > - The search box shows the live query text generated from checkbox/widget
  >   state and is directly editable — typed text re-parses with full AND/OR/NOT
  >   grammar and syncs back to the widgets where representable.
  > - Collapsible sections/groups (matching the sidebar's own ▾/▸ style) that
  >   auto-expand when something inside becomes selected, "only" links on brain
  >   rows, tri-state/master "select all" toggles, and a "has custom filters"
  >   icon+tooltip next to brains with a schema.
  > - Filters panel repositioned to fully cover the left BRAINS sidebar while
  >   open (was floating separately with a gap) — fixed positioning had to move
  >   the panel out of #search-wrap's DOM subtree, since a `transform` on an
  >   ancestor turns position:fixed into being relative to THAT ancestor instead
  >   of the viewport.
  > 
  > Backend: GET /schema/<repo>/<role> serves a brain's SCHEMA.json; /graph gains
  > schemaRoles (which brains have one) and per-node `num` (numeric facet field
  > values, generic prefix-scan so per-variant-suffixed keys are picked up too).
- neural-view: facet UI polish — +/- glyph, hover highlight, header fix, only-collapses-others (`be176d0`)
  > - Tri-state icon: a flex-centered +/- text glyph instead of a border-drawn
  >   checkmark/bar (which was never quite centered) — clearer "more/less" pairing.
  > - Facet and brain rows highlight on hover (subtle background tint).
  > - #sf-facets-heading was `justify-content:space-between` with the collapse
  >   chevron as its new first child, which shoved "Filters" to the far right
  >   with an empty gap — same gap-free flex-start as every other header now.
  > - Clicking a brain row's "only" now also collapses every OTHER repo group
  >   (nothing left checked in them) instead of leaving the whole list expanded
  >   around the one thing actually selected.
- neural-view: compound facet shortcuts + reskin native checkboxes to match (`fdf4867`)
  > Schema-declared "shortcuts" (schema.shortcuts[]) render as an extra row
  > inside one named facet, toggling values across MULTIPLE facets at once —
  > e.g. fab-cli's card-vault now ships "Attack Action" (Type:Action AND
  > Subtype:Attack) inside the Type section, a combination players search for
  > constantly. 2-state (unselected/include) rather than tri-state: excluding a
  > compound preset is ambiguous (NOT(A AND B) != NOT A AND NOT B) so it's left
  > out rather than guessed at. State is derived from the underlying facets'
  > include sets on every render, not tracked separately, so it also lights up
  > correctly from a manual click on the individual values or a typed query.
  > 
  > Also reskins every remaining native checkbox in the popover (Search-in,
  > brain toggles, per-facet "select all") to the same cyan-+/amber-− visual
  > language as the tri-state value rows, instead of a native white/blue OS
  > checkbox — paint only, checked/indeterminate stay real checkbox state.
  > 
  > Fixed a latent bug along the way: syncFacetFilter/updateFacetToggleState/
  > applyQueryTermsFromText's `.sf-facetrow` queries weren't scoped to
  > `[data-tag]`, so a shortcut row (no tag of its own) would have polluted a
  > facet's include/exclude sets with an "undefined" tag once shortcuts existed.
- neural-view: checked native checkboxes show a checkmark, not + (`30a1586`)
  > + is reserved for the tri-state VALUE rows (.sf-tristate), where it
  > specifically pairs with - for include/exclude. A plain checked/unchecked
  > checkbox (Search-in, brain/facet "select all" toggles) only ever has two
  > real states, so it gets the ordinary checkmark instead of implying a third
  > "exclude" state that control doesn't have. Indeterminate (-) is unchanged.

  > * test(247): red tests for outcome multiplier + contested marker (SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.4/R7.5/R7.7)
  >

  > so it encodes today's behavior as the byte-identical baseline (G6). The

  > 
  > Adds a reusable outcome-window/tally helper (outcome_window_tallies, on top
  > of the retros.log clock cmd_prune already uses) so GL-004's status tallies
  > and GL-033's report can call the same reader. cmd_recall composes an
  > outcome multiplier into SEED activation only (spread math untouched): net
  > outcomes within the last N retros (methodology.outcomeWindow, default 3)
  > scale activation by 1.0 + methodology.outcomeMultiplierStep × net, floored
  > at 0.1; zero outcomes or a net-zero tally multiply by exactly 1.0, so the
  > golden fixture proves byte-identical output when outcomes.jsonl is absent
  > (G6). A note with >=1 useful AND >=1 corrected/dead_end within the window
  > renders "⚠ contested" in the full and one-liner tiers (title tier
  > untouched); budget accounting stays byte-exact. A malformed outcomes.jsonl

  > validation and then raises a TypeError inside outcome_window_tallies once
  > >=N retros exist (ts < cutoff on a non-str ts; tallies.setdefault on a
  > non-hashable slug), crashing recall with a traceback instead of honoring
  > R7.7's warn-once/exit-0/degrade-to-baseline contract. Red against the

  >

  > outcome_window_tallies(), which then raised TypeError -- on `ts < cutoff`
  > once >=N retros existed, or on `tallies.setdefault(slug, ...)` -- crashing
  > recall with a traceback instead of the R7.7 contract (warn once, disable
  > weighting, exit 0). Both slug and ts are now required to be str; a
  > wrong-type line flips `malformed` exactly like an unparseable line or an

- GL-005: shrink guard on brain-mutating commands (#269) (`6a19cb3`)
  > * test(249): shrink guard regression cases for brain-mutating prune (red)
  > 
  > Fixtures for the four AC scenarios (over-threshold refusal, --force
  > override, small-brain floor, configured fraction) plus a below-threshold
  > control that pins today's unmodified prune behavior. brain.py has no
  > shrink guard yet, so the destructive-case checks fail as expected.
  > 
  > * feat(249): shrink guard on brain-mutating commands
  > 
  > Add a shared _shrink_guard(kind, remove_keys, total_count, force,
  > fraction) helper in brain.py and wire it into cmd_prune's --apply path
  > (the only destructive verb today; any future one routes through the
  > same helper). Over methodology.shrinkGuardFraction (default 0.3) AND
  > the absolute floor of 5 items, the command refuses non-zero with a
  > would-remove summary and nothing written; --force proceeds with a loud
  > removal summary and still emits LinkPruned per link. Below the floor
  > or the fraction, behavior is byte-identical to before.
  > 
  > Threshold documented in project-config.schema.json
  > (methodology.shrinkGuardFraction).
  > 
  > Lesson: SPEC-GRAPHIFY.md §13 / §5.2 item 1 — graphify's incremental
  > update silently replaced a merged graph with a code-only rebuild
  > (-74% edges, Graphify-Labs/graphify#2053) and silently evicted
  > semantic nodes (#2056); pruning could also no-op on a path mismatch
  > (#2012). Brains are the accumulated judgment of the workflow, easy to
  > clobber before commit review — no maintenance path should be able to
  > silently discard disproportionate knowledge.
  > 
  > * docs(249): document prune --force in brain skill usage
  > 
  > * test(249): strict byte-identical assertion + threshold boundary pin (review round 1)
  > 
  > The "links.json byte-identical after refusal" check used check (grep -F a
  > multiline expected string against actual), which passes as soon as any
  > single shared line matches -- it never caught a partial removal. Replace
  > it with cmp against a pre-run snapshot file, which fails on any byte
  > difference including a trailing-newline change from an accidental
  > re-write. Verified non-vacuous by temporarily simulating a write on
  > refusal: the old assertion stayed green, the new one fails as expected
  > (not committed).
  > 
  > Also pins the "<=" threshold semantics: a fixture where remove/total is
  > exactly the default 30% (6/20) proceeds without --force -- only strictly
  > over the fraction refuses.
  > 
  > * docs(249): dedupe entity-index clause introduced by rebase conflict resolution
