  > corrected glyphs), prune candidacy for notes with >=K dead_end and 0 useful
  > (full history, not the retro window), candidacy clearing once useful>=1,
  > --apply-free writes-nothing preserved, K configurable via
  > methodology.outcomeDeadEndPruneThreshold, and malformed-outcomes.jsonl
  > tolerance (warn once, disable, never crash) for both new surfaces.
  > 
  > * feat(248): status subcommand outcome tallies + prune dead_end signal (SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.6)
  > 
  > Adds `brain.py status <role>`: per-note bullet lines (shared _note_line
  > renderer with `directory`, so a note with zero outcomes -- or a role whose
  > outcomes.jsonl is absent -- renders byte-identically to `directory`'s
  > existing line for it) plus a compact `3✓ 1✗ 1⚠` tally when outcomes exist.
  > 
  > Extends outcome_window_tallies() with a full_history=True mode (skips the
  > retro-window cutoff entirely) rather than writing a second outcomes.jsonl
  > parser -- reused by both `status` and `prune`'s new rule: a note with
  > >=K full-history dead_end outcomes and zero useful becomes a prune
  > candidate ("outcome rule: N× dead_end, 0 useful ..."). K defaults to 2,
  > configurable via methodology.outcomeDeadEndPruneThreshold (schema
  > documented). Recording one useful outcome clears the candidacy.
  > 
  > This rule is propose-only: it never participates in --apply's removal
  > path (which still only ever removes the pre-existing link-level
  > candidates), so it introduces no new shrink-guard-relevant destructive
  > surface -- `prune` without --apply continues to write nothing.
  > 
  > Malformed outcomes.jsonl: both new surfaces warn once and fall back to
  > {} tallies via a shared helper, reusing _read_outcomes's existing
  > wrong-type/malformed-line rejection rather than re-validating.
  > 
  > * docs(248): document status subcommand + retro-protocol pointer (SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.6)
  > 
  > skills/brain/SKILL.md: `status <role>` subcommand entry alongside the
  > other verbs. retrospective/SKILL.md + build-next/references/brains.md:
  > one-line pointer at the prune/graduate step so the orchestrator checks
  > `status` tallies before pruning.
  > 
  > * test(248): assert DIRECTORY.md stays byte-identical to outcome data (review round 1)
  > 
  > Team-lead constraint: DIRECTORY.md is a committed artifact regenerated by
  > `directory` -- tallies must never leak into it (only the new `status` verb
  > renders them), since outcome churn would otherwise dirty a committed file
  > on every recorded outcome. Uses a non-trivial 3/1-style tally fixture so
  > the assertion is real, not a vacuous zero-outcome case; already satisfied
  > by the existing implementation (directory calls _note_line with no tally
  > arg) -- this closes the coverage gap the review flagged.
  > 
  > * test(248): red tests for apply-block skip + strict before/after snapshot (review round 1)
  > 
  > - prune without --apply: move the before/after snapshot around the FIRST
  >   prune call, while flaky-lesson IS a live outcome-rule candidate -- the
  >   old snapshot point ran after (4b) had already cleared the only
  >   candidate, so it only proved the trivially-safe no-candidate case.
  > - apply/outcome-only: prune --apply with ONLY outcome-rule note candidates
  >   (zero link candidates) must not enter the link-removal machinery: no
  >   misleading "removed 0 link(s)", an explicit "0 link candidate(s);
  >   outcome candidates are propose-only" message, links.json and the note
  >   file byte-identical (shasum) after --apply. Two variants: links.json
  >   already exists (from an unrelated link) and links.json absent
  >   beforehand (must stay absent, never created by this path).
  > - full-history vs. window: dead_end outcomes stamped before the
  >   retro-window cutoff must still flag the note (the rule is deliberately
  >   full-history, not the window recall's ranking multiplier uses).
  > 
  > * fix(248): skip the link-removal apply block when there are no link candidates (review round 1)
  > 
  > prune --apply with ONLY outcome-rule note candidates (zero link
  > candidates) was still entering the link-removal branch: shrink-guarding
  > an empty list, calling save_links unconditionally (which would CREATE
  > links.json in a brain that never had one), and printing a misleading
  > "removed 0 link(s)". Reviewer reproduced live. Now prints "0 link
  > candidate(s); outcome candidates are propose-only (nothing written)"
  > and writes nothing when there are no link candidates to remove.
  > 
  > ---------
- workflow: serial delivery mode (methodology.serialDelivery) (#279) (`f9532ed`)
  > * test(272): serial delivery mode — picker WAIT gate + move-guard defense in depth (red)
  > 
  > Fixtures + section-serial-delivery.sh cover next.py returning WAIT (not PICK)
  > while a session task sits In progress/In review under methodology.serialDelivery,
  > and guard-board-move.sh blocking a manual move to "In progress" per the offline
  > board-cache.json (fail-open on a cache miss). Neither surface implements the
  > mode yet — 11 assertions fail.
  > 
  > * feat(272): serial delivery mode (methodology.serialDelivery)
  > 
  > next.py's picker now prints WAIT (never PICK) while any board task sits
  > In progress or In review under serialDelivery — a task leaves In review
  > only by merging, so this gates on merge rather than lane width, orthogonal
  > to maxInProgress. guard-board-move.sh adds defense in depth: it blocks a
  > manual `board.sh move <n> "In progress"` when the offline board-cache.json
  > (#78, no network call) shows another task already In progress/In review,
  > with SERIAL_DELIVERY_OVERRIDE=1 as a documented escape hatch and fail-open
  > (warn, allow) on a cache miss so a stale/absent cache never wedges the loop.
  > 
  > Schema documents the new methodology.serialDelivery key.
  > 
  > * docs(272): document serialDelivery in the concurrency and build-next skills
  > 
  > concurrency SKILL.md gets a paragraph on how serialDelivery relates to
  > maxInProgress (orthogonal: width cap vs. merge gate); build-next SKILL.md's
  > Operating Rule 8 gets a pointer.
  > 
  > * docs(272): ask about serialDelivery during setup-project Phase 4
  > 
  > Adds a structured-input prompt alongside the existing merge-policy question,
  > off by default, pointing at the concurrency skill for the maxInProgress
  > trade-off.
  > 
  > * test(272): review round 1 fix pair — RESUME/WAIT split, compound-command guard, docs (red)
  > 
  > MUST FIX #1: an In-progress item must RESUME (never WAIT — WAIT with nothing
  > In progress to work on would deadlock the loop); WAIT only fires when In
  > review is the sole blocker; both present -> RESUME wins, In-review blocker
  > becomes a trailing NOTE line. New items.serial-both.json fixture covers the
  > combined case.
  > 
  > MUST FIX #3: guard-board-move.sh's evaluate() returns on the first board.sh
  > match, so a compound command's second segment (e.g. a progress-move after an
  > earlier review-move) never gets its own serial check. New regression: a
  > valid gate pass for the first segment must not mask a blocked second
  > segment.
  > 
  > MUST FIX #4: _serial_repo appended a second top-level `methodology:` block
  > (YAML last-wins silently drops tdd/isolationSuite/maxInProgress) instead of
  > merging into the existing one; fixed to merge in place. Pinned the
  > already-correct self-retry behavior (re-moving #N while #N itself is the
  > only cached In-progress entry must not self-block) as an explicit regression
  > test.
  > 
  > MUST FIX #2 (docs-with-behavior): assertions for the WAIT decision added to
  > build-next SKILL.md's Operating Rule 1 vocabulary and a WAIT protocol
  > paragraph in next-task SKILL.md — neither exists yet.
  > 
  > 11 assertions fail pre-fix.
  > 
  > * fix(272): review round 1 — RESUME/WAIT split, compound-command guard, docs
  > 
  > MUST FIX #1: next.py now computes wip/review_wip up front. An In-progress
  > item always RESUMEs (folded into the existing maxInProgress resume guard,
  > which serialDelivery now triggers even below the configured limit) — never
  > WAIT, since resuming/finishing in-flight work is the correct next action and
  > a WAIT with nothing In progress to work on would deadlock the loop. WAIT
  > fires only when In review is the SOLE blocker (nothing In progress). When
  > both are present, RESUME wins and the In-review item is reported as a
  > trailing NOTE line, not a second WAIT.
  > 
  > MUST FIX #3: guard-board-move.sh's evaluate() collects every board.sh match
  > in a (possibly compound) command instead of returning on the first one, so
  > an earlier review-move segment can no longer shadow a later progress-move's
  > own serial-delivery check. Each progress-move found is checked independently
  > against the cache; a block on any one blocks the whole command. A
  > review-move anywhere on the line still routes to gate-preflight as before.
  > 
  > Docs: build-next SKILL.md's Operating Rule 1 adds WAIT to the PICK/RESUME/
  > BLOCKED/PREFLIGHT FAIL decision vocabulary; next-task SKILL.md gets the
  > operator protocol (check the named PR's merge state via `gh pr view`; merged
  > -> move to QA, fold spec-delta, re-run next; still open -> genuine wait,
  > report and idle).
  > 
  > Also: fixed the _serial_repo test helper (MUST FIX #4) to merge
  > serialDelivery into the existing methodology: block instead of appending a
  > second top-level key (YAML last-wins was silently dropping tdd/
  > isolationSuite/maxInProgress), and pinned the already-correct self-retry
  > behavior as an explicit regression test.
  > 
  > Full suite green, shellcheck -x clean, gate pass re-recorded.
  > 
  > * fix(272): correct setup-project's serialDelivery description post round-1 fix
  > 
  > The "On" option text still described the pre-fix behavior (refuse to
  > proceed while ANY task is In progress/In review). Updated to match the
  > RESUME/WAIT split from the round-1 fix: resuming an already-In-progress
  > task is allowed, only picking/starting a NEW task is refused.
  > 
  > * docs(272): align concurrency-skill + schema serialDelivery wording with the RESUME/WAIT split
  > 
  > Both still described the pre-fix behavior ("refuse ... while ANY board task
  > is In progress or In review"). Updated to match: blocking applies to
  > picking a NEW task; resuming an already-In-progress task stays allowed
  > (that's finishing, not picking); an In-review task clears only by merging.
  > schema-lint's hover-completeness check (no literal-text pin) stays green.
  >

  > * test(276): ensure-serial-delivery rule cases (red)

  > /api/state now carries hubRev (hash of the hub page) and per-decision rev

  > Tier-1 wins from the framework/ecosystem research:
  > - hooks/hooks.json: SessionStart bootstrap (spec-workflow status + standing
  >   rules injected from message one; silent in unconfigured repos) and a
  >   PreToolUse(Bash) guard that BLOCKS 'board.sh move ... In review' unless
  >   gate.sh recorded a pass for the exact current tree (HEAD + uncommitted
  >   diff); any edit invalidates the pass, red gates clear it
  > - gate.sh wrapper (records passes) + tree-state.sh fingerprint; gate skill
  >   now mandates the wrapper — enforcement moved from prose to harness
  > - craft-spec: acceptance criteria in EARS notation (WHEN/WHILE/IF-THEN/WHERE
  >   ... THE SYSTEM SHALL ...), checklist tightened to match
  > - ui-options: template shuffles option order per load; no 'Suggested' badge
  >   in-page (recommendation goes in the issue comment) — kills position and
  >   endorsement bias (Design Arena pattern)
  > - implement-task: two-pass review (spec compliance, then code quality)
  > - tests: 13 new hermetic cases for the enforcement chain + session hook
